subject: Urgent: Surge-induced rejections from rate-window handoff
messages:
From: Samira Khan <samira.khan@astrolabs.com>
To: olga_petrov@redwood.com
Date: 2029-10-20T08:15:00Z
Subject: Repeated 429s and latency spikes during handoff windows

Hi Olga,

We started seeing elevated 429 responses and rising tail latency this morning between 07:50-08:10 PT. It looks correlated with our scheduled batch handoffs to a downstream service — traffic bursts cause a cascade of retries from our side.

Attached is a small sample of API responses and times. Requests that previously returned in ~90ms are now 700-1200ms or getting 429s. Our customer dashboards are showing error-side alerts. Can you confirm whether this is traffic shaping on Redwood's side or something in our integration? This is impacting our customers.

Thanks,
Samira
Head of Integrations, AstroLabs

Attachments: astrolabs-token-429-sample-log.txt

Samira —

Thanks for the quick flag and the sample logs. I'm looping in Ben (your AM) and our on-call infra engineer. We'll triage immediately and share a plan in the next hour.

— Olga

Samira, attaching the dashboard showing the spike (peak-traffic-dashboard.png).

Ben Carter

From: connor_obrien@redwood.com
To: ben_carter@redwood.com, olga_petrov@redwood.com
Cc: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com
Date: 2029-10-20T10:12:00Z
Subject: Re: Repeated 429s and latency spikes during handoff windows

Ben / Olga —

I've pulled server-side traces. Summary: during the 07:50-08:05 PT window we see a short-lived overlap between two quota windows for AstroLabs' tenant that causes their available burst credits to be deducted twice for a subset of requests. The overlap is due to a timing mismatch between our legacy per-tenant rolling-window selector and the newer token-bucket service. Net result: effectively halved burst capacity for ~90s which aligns with the 429 spike. Post-window, autoscaling mitigated latency, but the retry storms on the client side amplified load.

Immediate recommendation: 1) Apply a temporary override to unify AstroLabs' quota window (set unified-window=true) to eliminate overlap; 2) Increase their short-term burst allowance by 200% for 30 minutes to drain the retry queue; 3) Schedule a root-cause patch to the window selector (non-blocking deploy).

I can run step 1+2 now if we have approval. Logs attached to the JIRA.

Connor O'Brien
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference
From: olga_petrov@redwood.com
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com, connor_obrien@redwood.com
Cc: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com
Date: 2029-10-20T10:25:00Z
Subject: Fwd: Immediate mitigation for AstroLabs — need exec sign-off for temporary quota bump

Marissa —

Connor's diagnosis indicates a rate-window handoff overlap that halved AstroLabs' burst pool for ~90 seconds, triggering 429s and causing their retry traffic to spike our backend load. Connor proposes a temporary unified-window override and a 200% burst uplift for 30 minutes while we clear their retry backlog.

Given this is a live customer-impacting outage and tied to an enterprise account (DL-8792), I recommend approving the temporary increase. We're prepared to revert immediately after 30 minutes and to provide audit logs.

Key stakeholders: Ben (AM), Connor (SRE), Stephanie (Ops).

Olga
